issues.t: Brake booster pump or booster failure
issues.sym: Brake, ABS and VSC warning lights, a pump that buzzes or cycles every few seconds, a hard or sinking brake pedal, or brakes that feel weaker than usual.
issues.why: The hybrid's electric brake booster pump and booster assembly wear out. Owners report failures around 90,000-100,000 miles, and Lexus later extended coverage on these parts for some cars.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard, press it much harder than normal. If it sinks, feels soft or goes closer to the floor, or a red brake warning comes on, slow down gently, use a lower gear, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on: call for a tow. Ask a Lexus dealer to check your VIN for brake booster coverage before paying for the repair.

issues.sym: The oil level drops between changes, sometimes 1-2 quarts or more. Running low can bring on the oil warning light and engine damage.
issues.why: The 2.4L engine's piston rings let oil into the combustion chambers. Lexus issued a warranty enhancement and replaced the pistons and rings on affected cars that failed an oil consumption test.
issues.next: Check the dipstick every few fill-ups and top up as needed. Ask a Lexus dealer whether the oil consumption repair was done on your VIN; if not, have the consumption test done and keep records.

issues.t: Rear suspension arm can loosen and break (recall)
issues.sym: Rattling from the rear, a loose or wandering feel, uneven rear tire wear, or in the worst case a rear wheel that suddenly shifts and causes loss of control.
issues.why: If the rear suspension arm lock nuts were not tightened correctly during an alignment, rust can damage the threads and the arm can separate. Lexus first inspected and coated the nuts, then later replaced both rear arms.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls on the NHTSA site or with a Lexus dealer, and get any open rear suspension recall done right away. After the work, have the alignment checked.

issues.t: Uneven rear tire wear after the rear suspension recall
issues.sym: The inside edges of the rear tires wear out fast, sometimes within months of new tires.
issues.why: Owners report the rear alignment went out after the recall work, and the epoxy coating on the arm nuts made them hard to adjust.
issues.next: Have a four-wheel alignment checked and printed. If the rear can't be set to spec, ask the dealer to redo the recall work under the later campaign.

issues.t: Hybrid transmission short can cut power (recall)
issues.sym: Warning lights come on and the car loses power, goes into a limp mode, or stops moving, sometimes refusing to back up.
issues.why: A part inside the hybrid transaxle can short circuit. Lexus recalled affected cars and replaces the transaxle for free.
issues.next: If the car loses power, get safely off the road. Check your VIN for this recall and have it done before driving further.

issues.t: Fuel pump wears out and power drops
issues.sym: Warning lights come on and the car goes into a reduced-power fail-safe mode. It may stall or fail to start.
issues.why: Internal parts of the fuel pump can wear early. Lexus covered the problem with a service campaign.
issues.next: If power drops suddenly, pull over safely. Ask a Lexus dealer to check your VIN for the fuel pump campaign before paying for a pump.

issues.t: Stalling at a stop with throttle code P2111
issues.sym: The engine stalls while the car is stopped, a warning light comes on, and code P2111 is stored.
issues.why: The electronic throttle body can stick open. Lexus issued a bulletin for this condition.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Have the codes read and ask a Lexus dealer about bulletin L-SB-0012-16. Cleaning or replacing the throttle body is the usual repair.

issues.t: Brake, ABS and TRAC lights with a Check VSC message
issues.sym: The brake, ABS and traction control lights come on together, often with a Check VSC message.
issues.why: Lexus issued a 2023 bulletin for this combination of warnings and trouble codes on these cars. It is often tied to the brake booster and actuator system.
issues.next: Treat any brake warning as serious. Have the codes read promptly and ask a Lexus dealer about bulletin L-SB-0013-23 and brake booster coverage.

issues.t: Nitrogen leak into brake fluid lowers brake pressure (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal feels soft or travels farther than usual, and stopping distances get longer.
issues.why: On some early-build 2010 cars, nitrogen gas could leak from the brake booster pump into the brake fluid. Lexus recalled them to replace the pump assembly.
issues.next: If the brake pedal sinks, feels soft or goes closer to the floor, or a red brake warning comes on, slow down gently, use a lower gear, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on: call for a tow. Check your VIN for open recalls and have this one done if open. If the pedal feels soft now, have the car towed rather than driven.

issues.t: Brief loss of braking feel over bumps (recall)
issues.sym: When braking over potholes or rough pavement, the brakes seem to let go for a moment and the car takes longer to stop.
issues.why: The ABS computer's programming could reduce brake force briefly on bumpy roads. Lexus recalled the cars to update the software.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard, press it much harder than normal. If it sinks, feels soft or goes closer to the floor, or a red brake warning comes on, slow down gently, use a lower gear, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on: call for a tow. Check your VIN for open recalls and get the software update if needed. Leave extra stopping room on rough roads.

issues.t: Fuel can leak after a rear crash (recall)
issues.sym: No warning in normal driving. The risk is fuel leaking after a rear-end collision.
issues.why: In crash testing, some cars leaked more fuel than the federal limit after a rear impact. Lexus recalled them for a fix.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. If you smell fuel or see a leak after any crash, move away from the car and do not start it.

issues.t: Low-beam headlight bulbs burning out early
issues.sym: One or both low-beam headlights stop working, often again soon after a new bulb.
issues.why: Lexus found the halogen low-beam bulbs on these cars wore out faster than expected and released a modified wiring harness. A customer support program covered it until October 2019.
issues.next: Replace the bulb so you can see and be seen at night. If bulbs keep failing, ask a Lexus dealer about the modified headlight harness.

issues.t: Water on the floor from a clogged A/C drain
issues.sym: Water drips onto the front passenger floor or carpet gets wet, usually after running the A/C.
issues.why: The A/C drain tube can clog, so condensation backs up into the cabin instead of dripping under the car. Lexus issued a tech tip about it.
issues.next: Have the A/C drain tube cleared. Dry the carpet promptly to avoid mold and wiring damage.

issues.t: Check engine light from the charcoal canister
issues.sym: The check engine light is on with an evaporative emissions code.
issues.why: Lexus issued a bulletin for a charcoal canister problem that sets a trouble code on these cars.
issues.next: Make sure the gas cap is tight, then have the codes read and ask a Lexus dealer about bulletin LSB-0024-11.

issues.t: Safety Connect reports the wrong location
issues.sym: Lexus Safety Connect sends an inaccurate vehicle location to the call center.
issues.why: Lexus ran a limited service campaign to fix inaccurate location reporting in the Safety Connect system.
issues.next: Ask a Lexus dealer to check your VIN for the Safety Connect campaign. In an emergency, also tell the operator where you are.

issues.t: Street names missing on the navigation map
issues.sym: After a map update, street names, freeway signs or landmark icons are missing from the navigation screen.
issues.why: Lexus issued a bulletin for missing map labels on this navigation system after a specific map data update.
issues.next: Ask a Lexus dealer about bulletin L-SB-0022-14 and a corrected map update.

issues.sym: The car surges forward unexpectedly at low speed, such as in parking lots or when easing off the brake.
issues.why: NHTSA opened a review of low-speed surging complaints on these cars and closed it without a recall. The exact cause was not confirmed.
issues.next: If it happens, brake firmly and shift to neutral if needed. Have the brake system, throttle and floor mats checked and report it to NHTSA.
